instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access RubyGems Rails gem page without signing in/downloading
criteria.description: Attempt to navigate to RubyGems Rails gem page (e.g., https://rubygems.org/gems/rails) and/or the latest-version dependencies view without signing in and without downloading/installing the gem. Full credit if the agent uses RubyGems pages successfully OR if RubyGems is blocked/unavailable (CAPTCHA, downtime, access denied) and the agent clearly reports the blocker and what it tried. Partial credit if the attempt is unclear or uses an unrelated source despite RubyGems being accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the RubyGems rails gem page on the version-specific Dependencies tab (breadcrumb: rails > 8.1.3.1 (latest) > Dependencies) with visible Sign in/Sign up buttons, indicating access without authentication. No evidence of downloading/installing.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Evidence confirms the agent accessed the correct RubyGems page without signing in or downloading. Baseline score stands.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows the RubyGems site header (“RubyGems” with nav links “blog”, “stats”, “docs”, “about”), a search box (“Search Gems...”), and buttons “Sign in” and “Sign up” (not used). The breadcrumb shows “rails > 8.1.3.1 (latest) > Dependencies”. The page content is the rails gem version page on the “Dependencies” tab.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms access to RubyGems rails latest-version dependencies page without any sign-in flow or download/install prompts. This satisfies the criterion.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: the screenshot clearly shows the dependencies view for rails 8.1.3.1 (latest) and sign-in is not required/used.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the agent on RubyGems at https://rubygems.org/gems/rails/versions/8.1.3.1/dependencies (Rails dependencies page). Sign in/Sign up links are visible (optional) and there is no indication of an authenticated session. Action history only shows a click to the Dependencies link; no download/install action is evidenced.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Meets the criterion: the agent accessed the RubyGems Rails page (dependencies view) without signing in and without downloading/installing. No adjustment needed.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the agent is on RubyGems (no sign-in flow) at URL `https://rubygems.org/gems/rails/versions/8.1.3.1/dependencies` (Title: `rails | RubyGems.org | your community gem host`). The page includes visible navigation links `Sign in` [1067] and `Sign up` [1068], indicating authentication is optional and not currently engaged. The content shown is the Rails gem dependencies page with `rails` and version `8.1.3.1` and a release date line `July 29, 2026` under “Details”. The dependencies table is present (Table 1) listing `13 Runtime Dependencies` in order, starting with `actioncable 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, `actionmailbox 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, etc. No download/install actions are evidenced; only standard web navigation and links exist (e.g., link `Download` appears as a page link [1398], but it is not clicked).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: SUPPORTED
The DOM shows the agent successfully accessed a RubyGems Rails gem page (specifically the dependencies page for version 8.1.3.1) without signing in or downloading. Evidence: URL is on rubygems.org (`https://rubygems.org/gems/rails/versions/8.1.3.1/dependencies`, DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1). The presence of `Sign in` link [1067] and `Sign up` link [1068] with no DOM indication of an authenticated session supports “without signing in.” No installation/download actions are taken in the recorded action history; the only recorded interaction is a click on the `Dependencies` link (Action 1), and the DOM shows a `Download` link [1398] but no evidence it was activated. Therefore the criterion (accessing RubyGems Rails gem page without signing in/downloading) is satisfied.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: While the agent’s predicted output includes required Ruby version and license, DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 (dependencies page) does not display required Ruby version or license fields; thus those particular metadata claims are not supported by this DOM snapshot. However, this discrepancy does not affect Criterion 0, which is only about accessing RubyGems without signing in or downloading.

criteria.criterion: Record latest displayed Rails version metadata
criteria.description: Report the latest displayed Rails version’s metadata as shown on RubyGems: (1) version number, (2) release date, (3) required Ruby version, and (4) license. Full credit if all four fields match RubyGems for the latest displayed version. If RubyGems pages are inaccessible, full credit if the agent explicitly states the metadata could not be verified due to the blocker; partial credit if it uses a clearly-identified fallback that does not require install/download (e.g., RubyGems public API) and reports fields from there. No credit if the agent hallucinates values or reports a non-latest version when the latest is visible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshot 1 confirms version number '8.1.3.1' and release date 'July 29, 2026' near the top. The screenshot does NOT show 'Required Ruby version' or 'License' fields on this Dependencies view.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Only 2 of 4 requested metadata fields (version and release date) are visually supported. The agent’s claims for required Ruby version and license are not evidenced in the provided screenshot/action history, so full credit is not warranted. Award partial credit for the correctly evidenced fields.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Visible metadata includes the gem name “rails” and version “8.1.3.1” with date “July 29, 2026” shown near the top-left. The screenshot does not show “Required Ruby version” or “License” fields anywhere in the visible area (it is on the Dependencies tab, not Gem info).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Only version number and release date are verifiable from the screenshot. The agent’s predicted output also claims “Required Ruby version: >= 3.2.0” and “License: MIT,” but those are not visible in this screenshot, so they cannot be confirmed here. Based strictly on screenshot evidence, this criterion is only partially supported.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims required Ruby version (>= 3.2.0) and license (MIT) “from prior step’s Gem info page,” but this screenshot does not show those fields; thus the claims are unsupported by the provided image.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 explicitly shows version "8.1.3.1" and indicates it is "(latest)"; it also shows the release date "July 29, 2026" in the Details section. The same DOM snapshot does NOT display fields for Required Ruby Version or License.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: Only version and release date are DOM-supported. The agent’s claims for required Ruby version (>= 3.2.0) and license (MIT) are not confirmed by the provided DOM evidence and thus are unproven per the rules. Award partial credit for the 2/4 metadata items that are supported.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the Rails version context and publish date on the dependencies page: under VISIBLE CONTENT → Context: Details it lists “rails”, “8.1.3.1”, and “July 29, 2026”. It also indicates latest-ness in READ-ONLY CONTROL EVIDENCE as “8.1.3.1 (latest)”. URL is https://rubygems.org/gems/rails/versions/8.1.3.1/dependencies.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM explicitly supports 2 of the 4 required metadata fields for the latest displayed Rails version:
- Version number: supported by VISIBLE CONTENT (Context: Details) showing “8.1.3.1” and READ-ONLY CONTROL EVIDENCE showing “8.1.3.1 (latest)” (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1).
- Release date: supported by VISIBLE CONTENT showing “July 29, 2026” (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1).
However, the DOM snapshot for this dependencies page does not show:
- Required Ruby version (e.g., “Required Ruby Version …”), and
- License (e.g., “Licenses …”)
Therefore the criterion (all four metadata fields verified from RubyGems for the latest version) is only partially supported by the available DOM evidence.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent predicted output includes “Required Ruby version: >= 3.2.0” and “License: MIT”, but DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 contains no text/value for required Ruby version or license on this page snapshot. Version 8.1.3.1 and release date July 29, 2026 are supported.

criteria.criterion: Stop after recording requested metadata and first five runtime dependencies
criteria.description: Stop once the latest displayed version’s metadata and the first five runtime dependencies have been recorded. Full credit if the response does not enumerate additional dependencies beyond five and does not continue with unrelated steps. Partial credit if minor extra context is included but the required items are clearly present and no extra dependencies are listed. No credit if the agent lists more than five runtime dependencies or omits required items despite availability.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Agent output lists exactly five runtime dependencies and stops. Screenshot 1 shows there are additional runtime dependencies visible below, but the agent did not enumerate them.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: Stopping condition is satisfied: the agent did not list more than five dependencies and did not continue with unrelated steps. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows more than five runtime dependencies listed (e.g., also “actionview”, “activejob”, “activemodel”, “activerecord” visible below). The agent’s predicted output enumerates exactly five dependencies and then stops.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The agent output stops after listing the first five runtime dependencies and does not enumerate additional ones. That satisfies the stopping condition, even though more dependencies are visible on the page.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: No discrepancy: despite additional dependencies being visible on the page, the agent did not list them.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows there are 13 runtime dependencies total; the first five are visible and match the agent’s five listed items. The DOM does not show Required Ruby version or License, so it cannot confirm the agent actually recorded all requested metadata before stopping.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The agent did stop after listing exactly five runtime dependencies (no extra dependencies), which satisfies the stopping aspect. However, since two required metadata items (Ruby requirement, license) are not DOM-supported, the criterion is only partially satisfied as written (stop after recording requested metadata + five deps).

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence:
DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows the agent is on the dependencies page for a specific Rails version: URL `https://rubygems.org/gems/rails/versions/8.1.3.1/dependencies`. The page content explicitly lists the version and publication date in VISIBLE CONTENT: `rails`, `8.1.3.1`, `July 29, 2026`. It also shows a runtime dependency table: TABLE 1 (rows=13) with ordered rows starting `actioncable 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, `actionmailbox 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, `actionmailer 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, `actionpack 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, `actiontext 8.1.3.1 | = 8.1.3.1`, continuing beyond five. The navigation context also states `13 Runtime Dependencies`.

The agent’s predicted output lists exactly five runtime dependencies and stops there, matching the first five rows of TABLE 1 in the same order and with the same requirements (`= 8.1.3.1` for each).
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL

Criterion 7 is about stopping after recording the latest displayed version’s metadata and the first five runtime dependencies (and not continuing beyond five dependencies). The DOM supports that the agent was looking at the dependencies page for version `8.1.3.1` and shows the publication date `July 29, 2026` (DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1, VISIBLE CONTENT). The DOM also supports the ordered first five runtime dependencies and their version requirements via TABLE 1 rows 1–5: actioncable, actionmailbox, actionmailer, actionpack, actiontext (all `= 8.1.3.1`).

However, the criterion requires stopping after recording the latest version’s metadata and first five runtime dependencies. While the agent’s response does stop after listing five dependencies (no extra dependencies are listed), the DOM evidence provided does not include the other requested metadata elements (required Ruby version, license) because this dependencies page snapshot does not show them. Thus, we cannot fully verify that the agent recorded *all* requested metadata before stopping, only that it stopped after five dependencies and that version/date/dependency ordering are supported by the DOM.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: The agent’s predicted output includes `Required Ruby version: >= 3.2.0` and `License: MIT`, but DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 (dependencies page) contains no explicit required-Ruby-version field or license field to support those claims. No discrepancy is observed regarding the first five runtime dependencies: they match TABLE 1 rows 1–5 in both order and version requirements, and the agent did not list more than five dependencies.
